title: Model surge containment and staged telemetry rewind for mixed-deployment regressions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
A subset of recent model rollouts produced a short-lived but high-frequency quality degradation pattern limited to mixed-deployment tenants (Hosted + Dedicated) and surfaced as elevated user complaints and a 12% uplift in error tokens for a small cohort. This ticket coordinates containment, production bugfixes, and a staged telemetry 'rewind' to recover and validate model behavior across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope and goals:
- Contain active customer impact within 30 minutes for affected slices.
- Restore stable model behavior or safe fallback for all tenants within 3 hours of detection.
- Reconcile KV cache and prefix state between model variants to prevent sticky regressions.
- Produce reproducible telemetry replay artifacts for postmortem and regression tests.

Why this is different:
Most rollback playbooks focus on traffic shift or model reversion. This incident includes a surge artifact: a combination of transient input distribution shift + aggressive KV cache priming that amplifies specific prompt prefixes in Dedicated pools but not in Hosted. Containment requires coordinated runtime toggles, selective cache drains, and a telemetry rewind that can replay sampled requests against candidate fixes without impacting live traffic.

Runbook (high level):
1) Detection and slice identification (SRE): query anomaly dashboard for signal vector (response drift, token error rate, latency spikes) and tag tenant slices.
2) Fast containment (SRE + Runtime): enable per-tenant model pin to last-known-good variant for Hosted and Dedicated; apply temporary request-throttling for noisy tenants.
3) KV cache neutralization (Runtime): for affected Dedicated pools, perform targeted KV cache invalidation for the model family and sequence-length cohorts; for Hosted, enable 'ignore-prefix-cache' flag for 10m to avoid re-priming.
4) Telemetry rewind (Observability): stream-sample 1% of affected requests to the rewind pipeline; run them against a staging candidate (quantization patch + kernel ordering change) and the pinned baseline, collect diffs.
5) Patch rollout (Eng): stage a conservative patch (kernel reordering and soft-quant tune) to a single Dedicated plane slice; monitor metrics and customer contacts for 60m.
6) Controlled expansion (Eng + PM): if stable, expand patch to remaining Dedicated slices and a light-weight Hosted canary; if not, revert staged patch and escalate.
7) Customer comms (Support + Field Engineering): open customer-facing incident notes, include expected timelines and recovery actions, assign field liaison for top-10 affected customers.

Technical mitigation options evaluated and tradeoffs:
- Full model reversion: fastest to restore but loses forward progress and may break compatibility with new kernel optimizations.
- Selective KV drain + pin: lowest blast radius but requires careful per-pool orchestration.
- Runtime kernel fallback (non-quantized path): preserves newer model but increases latency/cost.
Decision: begin with selective KV cache neutralization + tenant pin to baseline; simultaneously test a small kernel-ordering patch in staging for a potential safe forward fix.

Artifacts and links:
- Repro harness (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/model-surge-repro-harness (sampling plan, replay instructions)
- Telemetry query: https://observability.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/model-surge-vector (dashboard with slice filters)
- Draft PR for kernel ordering patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128
- Customer incident notes template: https://drive.redwood.ai/incident-templates/model-surge-customer-note.docx

Acceptance criteria:
- Affected tenant slice error-token-rate reduced to baseline ±5% for 2 consecutive 30m windows.
- No more than 5 active customer escalations remaining (field liaison assigned).
- Rewind-run diffs collected and stored in replay bucket, with a reproducible pipeline to run candidate fixes.
- Postmortem draft started with timelines and root-cause hypotheses.

Rollout choreography checklist (taskable items):
- SRE: identify tenant slices, update incident channel, run initial containment toggles.
- Runtime Eng: implement per-pool KV drain script and safe 'ignore-prefix-cache' flag.
- Observability: enable rewind sampling and build a replay job for the candidate patch.
- QA: run replayed requests against baseline and candidate; provide quality metrics.
- Support: prepare customer notes and coordinate field liaisons.
- PM: approve canary expansion criteria and customer comms language.

Notes on Dedicated vs Private differences:
- Dedicated: has pool-level KV caches and pinned variants per pool — we can target drains at pool id and tenant slices.
- Private: customers may run on-prem variants; we must provide a self-serve patch bundle and detailed steps rather than automatic cache drains. Coordinate with Solutions Engineering for private tenant support.

Observability signals to watch during remediation:
- response_quality_delta (token-level semantic regression score)
- per-tenant error_token_rate and latency_percentiles (p50/p95/p99)
- KV cache hit ratio by pool and prefix cohort
- customer_contact_rate and top-10 complaint reasons

Postmortem hypotheses to explore:
- kernel ordering mismatch interacting with a spike in short-context prompts
- aggressive KV priming in Dedicated pools exposing a quantization edge case
- race between autoscaling/dedicated pool handoff and model variant pinning
